title: Harden a Pod with SecurityContext
description: Run a Pod with non‑root user, read‑only root filesystem, and dropped capabilities.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal
Create a Pod that runs securely with the following SecurityContext settings:
- Run as user ID 1000, group ID 2000.
- Ensure `runAsNonRoot: true`.
- Drop all Linux capabilities, add only `NET_BIND_SERVICE` (for nginx to bind port 80).
- Mount root filesystem as read‑only.
- But nginx needs to write to `/var/cache/nginx` and `/var/run`. So add emptyDir volumes for those paths.

### Steps
1. Write a Pod YAML `secure-nginx.yaml` with:
   - name: `secure-nginx`
   - container image: nginx:1.25
   - pod securityContext: `runAsUser: 1000`, `runAsGroup: 2000`, `fsGroup: 2000`.
   - container securityContext:
     - `runAsNonRoot: true`
     - `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true`
     - `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`
     - `capabilities: drop: ["ALL"], add: ["NET_BIND_SERVICE"]`
   - volumes: two emptyDir volumes named `cache-vol` and `run-vol`.
   - volumeMounts: mount `cache-vol` at `/var/cache/nginx`, `run-vol` at `/var/run`.
2. Apply the Pod.
3. Verify the Pod is Running. If it crashes, check the logs – likely missing writable directories; adjust volume mounts.
4. Exec into the Pod: `kubectl exec -it secure-nginx -- sh`.
   - Run `whoami` – should show `1000` (or `whoami` not found, try `id`).
   - Run `touch /test-file` – should fail with read‑only filesystem.
   - Run `touch /var/cache/nginx/test-file` – should succeed.
5. Delete the Pod.
hints: Nginx official image runs as root by default, but by setting `runAsUser: 1000` we force it to run as non‑root. Nginx's master process starts as root and workers as configured user; so you might need to set nginx.conf to listen on port >1024 if you drop NET_BIND_SERVICE, but we added it so it can still use port 80. However, running nginx as non‑root master requires the binary to be able to bind; with NET_BIND_SERVICE it works.
If the container fails to start, check the Events with `kubectl describe pod` – maybe missing writable dir `/var/run`. Add an emptyDir for `/var/run` as well.
The `fsGroup` ensures that volumes are writable by group 2000, so user 1000 can write to them if group permissions allow.
expectedOutput: Pod runs; `id` shows uid 1000; writing to root fails, writing to mounted volumes succeeds.
solutionCode:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: secure-nginx
spec:
  securityContext:
    runAsUser: 1000
    runAsGroup: 2000
    fsGroup: 2000
  volumes:
  - name: cache-vol
    emptyDir: {}
  - name: run-vol
    emptyDir: {}
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.25
    securityContext:
      runAsNonRoot: true
      readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      capabilities:
        drop: ["ALL"]
        add: ["NET_BIND_SERVICE"]
    volumeMounts:
    - name: cache-vol
      mountPath: /var/cache/nginx
    - name: run-vol
      mountPath: /var/run
